name: action-switching
title: Action Switching in Embodied Agents (Agmon & Beer 2014)
lead:
This is the capstone brain-body-environment model and the only one with
internal metabolic state. The agent must do more than chemotax: it must sense
its own two nutrient levels, and when one runs low, disengage from the resource
it is currently exploiting and navigate to the other — then switch back. The
interest is dynamical: how a small nervous system produces two different
coordinated actions and autonomous transitions between them.

at_a_glance.role: the agent forages both resources and outlives a non-mover
the dynamical signature of switching: anti-phase engagement + sawtooth nutrients
the three morphologies' sensing; M2 is the evolved/analyzed agent

glossary.definition: Autonomously changing which coordinated action is engaged (here: which resource is foraged) without a higher-level selector.
The agent's two nutrient levels, sensed internally and coupled to the environment via eating.
A sensor projecting 6 units from the body, reading a resource's chemical concentration at its tip.
A transient regime in which a subset of sensors/effectors drives a particular action (approach/eat A, or B).

biological_story:
An animal that needs two different nutrients cannot simply walk up one gradient
forever. It must notice, from the inside, that one reserve is running low, break
off whatever it is doing, and go get the other — then switch back. Agmon &
Beer's forager is the minimal creature that does this. Its single front stalk
smells both chemical signals, and two internal sensors report how full each
nutrient store is. When both are comfortable it exploits the nearer resource;
as the neglected store falls, the internal sensors tip the balance of the little
nervous system and the whole coupled system slides into a new mode of
coordination — heading for the other resource. The result, read off the
trajectories, is a clean alternation: the agent orbits from one resource to the
other and back, the two distances in anti-phase, each nutrient sawtoothing up
when fed and down when left. Nowhere is there a module that decides "now switch";
the switch is a transition in the flow of the brain-body-environment system,
which is exactly the point of the paper.
question:
Can a single CTRNN agent with internal metabolic state autonomously switch
between two foraging actions — approaching two different chemical resources to
keep two nutrient levels alive — purely through the dynamics of its coupled
brain-body-environment system, with no higher-level action-selection
mechanism?
hypothesis:
An agent evolved for longevity in a world with two depleting nutrients and two
gradient resources will shuttle between the resources, engaging whichever one
replenishes the nutrient that is currently low. The switch is not a discrete
decision but a transition in the coupled system's state driven by the internal
nutrient sensors, reproducing the action switching of Agmon & Beer (2014).

executive.what_is_this:
An evolved CTRNN forager (morphology M2: one front chemosensory stalk sensing
both chemical signals, plus two internal nutrient sensors; two force
effectors) in a bounded plane with two gradient resources, built on the shared
CTRNN brain. It is tasked with staying alive, which requires keeping both
nutrient levels above zero. The genome was evolved by the workspace's own GA
and committed; the studies replay it deterministically.
executive.verdict:
Reproduced. The evolved agent autonomously switches between the two resources
— it forages both in 12 of 16 FAR, high-drain environments (resources 42-62 units apart, with
orientation/size/start) — sustaining both nutrients far longer than a passive agent
ASYMMETRIC per-nutrient drain). Crucially it is STATE-DEPENDENT: it uses its internal nutrient sensors to prioritize the faster-draining resource. The
distance-to-resource traces are anti-phase and the nutrient traces sawtooth as
it alternates, the signature of action switching.
executive.verdict_detail:
From the committed seed (morphology M2, pop 100, gen 160, seed 0), verified in
the test suite: forages both resources in 12/16 FAR high-drain environments
(survival ~2098). The key behaviour is GENUINE STATE-DEPENDENT ACTION
SWITCHING (the paper's point): ablating the agent's internal nutrient sensors
measurably hurts it (+226 survival, +2 forages-both come from state-sensing),
and its trajectories show it CAMPING at whichever resource is draining fast,
which it can only know by sensing its own nutrient levels. This fixes an
earlier regime where the agent survived by BLIND CIRCLING that ignored the
nutrient sensors entirely (ablation changed nothing): with two close,
reachable resources, fast circling feeds both regardless of state, so there
was no pressure to use internal state. Making the resources FAR (sep 42-62)
with HIGH ASYMMETRIC drain (base 0.005, 1.3-1.8x, which nutrient is fast
alternates) makes a full round-trip away nearly starve the fast nutrient, so
equal-time circling fails and the agent must prioritize by state. Honest
scope: the switching is state-dependent but INCOMPLETE; it over-commits to the
urgent resource and sometimes lets the slow one slowly die (hence 12/16, not
16/16), and it is not immortal (nutrients net-decline, so it eventually
starves). ENABLING clean-room choices (not Agmon-Beer-exact): sped-up agent
(max_thrust 0.025), longer-range gradient (decay 0.03), eat 0.07, and the
far, high-drain battery.

decisions_needed.question: Report the M2 agent as the single analyzed agent (as the paper does), or also evolve M1/M3 for a full morphology comparison?
decisions_needed.context: The paper's deep dynamical analysis is of ONE morphology-2 agent. M1/M3 are presented here structurally; evolving them is a documented extension.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
Action switching in this agent is a property of brain-body-environment
dynamics coupled through internal metabolic state: the same sensorimotor loop
produces two different foraging actions and autonomous transitions between
them, with no internal action-selection arbiter.
evidence_for: Forages both resources in 12/16 FAR high-drain environments (sep 42-62, asymmetric drain), survival ~2098.

STATE-DEPENDENT: ablating the internal nutrient sensors costs +226 survival + 2 forages-both — the agent genuinely uses internal metabolic state (pinned in tests/test_forager_seed.py), prioritizing the faster-draining resource. The earlier blind-circling regime was ablation-insensitive (sensors unused).
Distance-to-A and distance-to-B are anti-phase; nutrient levels sawtooth in step with engagement (figures/action_switching.png).
Switching behaviour emerges over evolution (figures/evolution_curves.png): the share foraging both climbs toward 12/16 over evolution.
evidence_against: The agent is not immortal: both nutrients net-decline over a trial, so it eventually starves (~1-2.5k steps) rather than surviving indefinitely.
key_figures: figures/forage.gif — the agent shuttling between resources, with live nutrient bars
figures/action_switching.png — anti-phase distance traces + sawtooth nutrients (the switching signature)
figures/nutrient_phase.png — internal-state (nutrient A vs B) phase plot
figures/evolution_curves.png — switching behaviour emerging over evolution
caveats: Fitness used an opt-in balance term; the paper-faithful pure-longevity fitness is the default.

The battery makes BLIND CIRCLING non-viable (far resources + high asymmetric drain), which is what forces the agent to read internal state. Honest limit: state-dependent but incomplete (over-commits to the urgent resource -> 12/16).
A single evolved morphology-2 agent; M1/M3 are shown structurally, not evolved here.

studies.name: as-forage-and-survival
studies.title: Forage Both & Outlive a Non-Mover
studies.question: Does the evolved forager keep both nutrients alive by visiting both resources, and does it survive longer than a passive agent?

findings.summary: Forages both in 12/16 far high-drain environments (survival ~2098); STATE-DEPENDENT — prioritizes the fast-draining resource, ablation of the nutrient sensors costs +226 survival + 2 forages-both (was 0 for the old blind circler).
findings.detail: figures/forage.gif shows the agent shuttling between resources while both nutrient bars are sustained; figures/trajectory_nutrients.png shows the spatial loop + nutrient time series.

studies.claim: The agent forages both resources in 12 of 16 FAR, high-drain environments (sep 42-62, asymmetric per-nutrient drain) and is STATE-DEPENDENT: it uses its internal nutrient sensors to prioritize the faster-draining resource (ablating them costs +226 survival + 2 forages-both), rather than the blind circling of the earlier regime.

derived.insight: Forages both in 12/16 far high-drain environments (survival ~2098); STATE-DEPENDENT — prioritizes the fast-draining resource, ablation of the nutrient sensors costs +226 survival + 2 forages-both (was 0 for the old blind circler).

studies.name: as-switching-dynamics
studies.title: The Dynamical Signature of Switching
studies.question: What is the dynamical signature of the agent's action switching — how do its distance-to-resource and internal nutrient states evolve as it alternates?

findings.summary: ~9-10 alternating engagement cycles; nutrients sawtooth, sustained by switching (slow net decline).
findings.detail: figures/action_switching.png: shaded bands alternate red/green (engaged with A/B) in anti-phase; the nutrient panel shows each level rising on engagement. figures/nutrient_phase.png traces the switching cycle in internal-state space.

studies.claim: Distance to A and B are anti-phase and the nutrients sawtooth in step with engagement — the agent rhythmically switches between foraging the two resources.

derived.insight: ~9-10 alternating engagement cycles; nutrients sawtooth, sustained by switching (slow net decline).

studies.name: as-morphology-comparison
studies.title: Three Morphologies' Sensing
studies.question: How do the three morphologies differ in what they can sense, and which is the agent analyzed here?

findings.summary: M2 (one front stalk + nutrient sensors) is the evolved, switching agent; M1/M3 shown structurally.
findings.detail: figures/morphologies.png diagrams the three sensor layouts. M3 lacks internal nutrient sensors, so it would have to internalize nutrient state to switch — evolving M1/M3 is a documented extension.

studies.claim: The three morphologies differ in chemosensor placement and whether they have internal nutrient sensors; the evolved, analyzed agent is morphology M2 (one front stalk + nutrient sensors).

derived.insight: M2 (one front stalk + nutrient sensors) is the evolved, switching agent; M1/M3 shown structurally.
